title: Constructible rational modules admit finite open–closed lattice refinements
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $\Lambda=\underline E$, the condensed ring of continuous functions to normed $E$, or $\Lambda=\Omega^{\mathrm{fin}}$, whose sections on a profinite set are continuous functions to $\Omega$ with image in one finite subextension [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Put $\mathcal F=\{E\}$ in the first case and let $\mathcal F$ be all finite subextensions of $\Omega$ in the second. For $F\in\mathcal F$ write $A_F=\mathcal O_F$ with its norm topology. For each scheme $T$, use the pulled-back condensed coefficient rings $\Lambda_T,F_T,A_{F,T}$ on the small pro-étale site, module objects, and ordinary uncompleted unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-size-convention]. Constructibility means finite constant scalar models on a finite constructible locally closed stratification; $D_{\mathrm{ctf}}$ means bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. A lisse module is pro-étale locally free of finite rank. A scheme is qcqs when it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism].

Let $V$ be qcqs and $M$ a constructible $\Lambda_V$-module. There is a finite rooted binary tree of locally closed subschemes with root $V$, every internal vertex $T$ partitioned by a quasi-compact open immersion $U\hookrightarrow T$ and its complementary closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. All vertices are qcqs, every branch morphism is quasi-compact, and nonempty leaves partition $V$. Every leaf has an actual factoring scheme morphism to a stratum of a finite constructible stratification witnessing constructibility of $M$, and $M$ restricts to a lisse module on each leaf.

Moreover fix such a tree, and suppose that on every nonempty leaf $T$ one is given a finite constructible locally closed partition $T=\coprod_s S_{T,s}$, finite fields $F_{T,s}\in\mathcal F$, lisse $A_{F_{T,s},S_{T,s}}$-modules $B_{T,s}$ and isomorphisms $\Lambda_{S_{T,s}}\otimes_{A_{F_{T,s},S_{T,s}}}B_{T,s}\cong M|_{S_{T,s}}$. There is a finite refinement by trees of the same kind such that every new nonempty leaf $W$ has an actual factoring scheme morphism to one $S_{T,s}$. Pullback gives a lisse integral module $B_W$ and an isomorphism $\Lambda_W\otimes_{A_{F_{T,s},W}}B_W\cong M|_W$. Empty leaves can be given the zero module over $A_E$. The conclusion uses scheme morphisms and their coefficient pullbacks, not just containment of underlying subsets.

proof.text: Use finiteConstantLocalModel_iff_exists_cover and models_free_cover from det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model. Identify the scalar ring at the one-point profinite set with ULift E or ULift Omega by constant functions and evaluation. For Omega each constant is valued in the finite simple extension generated by its value. The monoidal sections multiplication is the sectionwise ring multiplication. Restrict along the scalar ring isomorphism and use internalToModule to identify finitely presented scalar modules with finite-dimensional vector spaces. Transport Module.finBasis through the equivalence and the finite-biproduct coordinates. Thus each original constant-model stratum is lisse, without any Noetherian assumption.

Reuse the finite pullback construction of lem-fix-constructible-open-closed-refinement-tree before its final numerical encoding: split a leaf by pullbacks of O and Z and its open child by pullbacks of Q and the given stratum. Scheme.Pullback.range_fst proves complementarity. Keep either avoidance or an actual factorization through each processed stratum; induct on the finite set of strata using SchemeRefinementTree.bind. Covering rules out avoidance on each nonempty final leaf. Forget the auxiliary allowed-split predicate by tree induction. Apply this construction to the constructibility stratification, then use canonical pullback composition and preservation of lissity to obtain the first assertion.

proof.text: For a new nonempty leaf choose its actual stratum factorization h and pull back the supplied integral module. CondensedRing.pullIso for the canonical integral coefficient inclusion identifies extension after pullback with pullback after extension; map the supplied scalar-extension isomorphism by upperStar and apply upperStarComp. The equation h followed by the stratum immersion equals the leaf map identifies the resulting target with M restricted to the leaf. This uses the already proved normalized underived Pull comparison rather than rebuilding its coefficient square. On every empty leaf all sheaves of modules vanish by the empty-cover sheaf condition. Zero is finite free of rank zero, its scalar extension is zero, and the unique zero-object isomorphism supplies the empty-leaf model. Retain CartesianCoefficients as an import on the mandated unit route; its untwisted comparison is incorporated in the existing normalized coefficient framework.

tool_uses.why: General qcqs scheme-theoretic finite refinement through original constructible strata, applied before and after the supplied lattice partitions; this geometric tool is absent from the compactification-coherence unit.
General preservation of pro-étale local finite freeness for any condensed ring and any scheme morphism; the unit has no such coefficient pullback lemma.

Ordinary internal extension of scalars commutes with inverse image for arbitrary commutative ring objects; needed to pull back each supplied lattice isomorphism without changing coefficient categories.

Untwisted coefficient-ring pullback isomorphisms for integral and rational coefficients, with no invertibility or Noetherian hypotheses; a generic coefficient tool, not a replacement for the unit route.
